title: Call for residency hosts 2026-2027
content:
The call for residency hosts provides financial support to legal entities wishing to host artists and cultural professionals for one residency project.

This call has two phases:

Submission of the application describing the residency project, together with the required supporting documents about the legal entity.

If selected in phase 1, applicants can proceed to choose the artists and cultural professionals who will be their residents. And then complete the second and final part of the application.

Legal entities that:

  • are registered and based in one of the Creative Europe countries, including the overseas countries and territories and outermost regions
  • have the capacity to host the proposed residency project with artists and cultural professionals from other Creative Europe countries
  • regardless of being a newly or well-established entity, applicants must be active in one of the eligible sectors: architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts, and visual arts

    • The residency grant offers financial support to the host and each resident:

    €50 per day, per resident.

title: Protesters Say India's Democracy Is "Rotten" as Modi Gov't Purges Voter Rolls, Arrests Thousands
content:
Tens of thousands of people in India have taken to the streets in recent days to protest the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls, a large majority of which are believed to be opposed to Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP party. The demonstrations, joined by leaders from India’s opposition parties, are being led by students and the youth-led “Cockroach” movement. Tens of thousands of security forces, including paramilitary and police, were out on the streets over the weekend cracking down on the uprising, detaining protesters en masse, including lawyers, journalists and protest leaders.

The demonstrations “represent an outpouring of anger, of frustration at what many Indians feel is the fact that their democracy has been taken away,” says Shoaib Daniyal, political editor of Scroll, who was arrested on Saturday along with 7,000 other protesters. He points out that “the deletions have affected Muslims far more than they have affected other Indians.”

title: Bangladesh-Malaysia recruitment reforms revive old questions over the cost of migration
content:
Repeated disruptions raise concerns over recruitment transparency and migrant workers’ protection from exploitation.

Originally published on Global Voices

On Saturday, October 5, 2024, a Memorandum of Collaboration (MOC) was signed in Dhaka between the Wage Earners Welfare Board and Malaysia's PERKESO, regarding the expansion of the labor market in Malaysia. Image via Wikipedia by Press Information Department of Bangladesh. Public Domain.

Officials in both Bangladesh and Malaysia’s have made repeated attempts to reform the countries’ labour migration relationship, leading to numerous suspensions and reopenings over more than three decades.

However, on August 30, 2026, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives, Mir Shahe Alam, announced that Malaysia would recruit around 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over six months, with departures expected to begin in late September. He also referred to a plan to send 10,000 workers without requiring them to bear migration costs.

title: Interview with Eleonora Alariesto – DJ Hulluella
content:
Before the interview begins, one question is already present: am I talking to Eleonora Alariesto or DJ Hulluella?

Dressed in an outfit that combines elements of traditional Sámi dress, gákti, handcrafted silver jewellery and colours symbolising her family ties in the Northern Sámi region, she has paired it with fishnet stockings, chunky leather boots and a denim cap decorated with fake diamonds.

The aesthetic mixture also reflects the diversity of both Eleonora Alariesto and the artistic universe of her creative alter ego, DJ Hulluella. It quickly becomes clear that the two exist at the same time, but in different roles.

Eleonora Alariesto is a freelance journalist, host of the podcast “Mii gullo…?” and producer, with most of her current projects connected in some way to Sámi culture.

title: Ulkoministeri Valtonen vaatii venäläisten turistiviisumien täyskieltoa EU:ssa
content:
Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen vaatii, että Euroopan unionin jäsenmaat lopettavat turistiviisumien myöntämisen Venäjän kansalaisille, kunnes Venäjä lopettaa hyökkäyssotansa. Ulkoministeri Valtonen peräänkuuluttaa koko EU:n yhteistä, tiukempaa viisumilinjaa.

Ulkoministeri Valtonen vaatii Euroopan komissiolta tiukempia suuntaviivoja Venäjän kansalaisten viisumihakemusten käsittelyyn sekä tarvittavia EU-lainsäädännön muutoksia turistiviisumikiellon toteuttamiseksi. 

Schengen-maiden venäläisille myöntämien turistiviisumien määrä on kasvanut viime vuosina. Vuonna 2025 Schengen-maat myönsivät venäläisille lähes 500 000 turistiviisumia. 

”Venäjän kansalaisille ei tule myöntää turistiviisumeja niin kauan kuin Venäjä jatkaa hyökkäyssotaansa. Venäjä hyökkää Ukrainaan nyt jo viidettä vuotta. Ei ole oikein, että venäläiset nauttivat eurooppalaisen elämäntavan iloista ja vapauksista samalla kun heidän maansa pommittaa ukrainalaisten koteja”, ulkoministeri Valtonen sanoo.  

”Suomessa kiellettiin viisumien myöntäminen venäläisille ei-välttämätöntä matkustusta varten valtioneuvoston periaatepäätöksellä jo vuonna 2022”, ulkoministeri Valtonen jatkaa. ”Sama tulee vihdoin tehdä EU-tasolla.”

title: Croatia Expands Probe Into Alleged Multi-Million-Euro Toxic Waste Scheme
content:
Croatia's anti-corruption office, USKOK, expanded its investigation into an alleged international illegal waste dumping ring, arresting and questioning five new suspects and three companies over the suspected criminal disposal of hazardous materials near the town of Benkovac and inside the Velebit Nature Park near Senj.

The suspects were released after questioning, as USKOK stated there were no legal grounds to request pre-trial detention. Friday's action marks the third expansion of the sweeping environmental crime probe, which now targets a total of 14 individuals and four companies suspected of severe environmental crimes and falsifying official documents within a criminal enterprise.

The investigation, supported by Europol and law enforcement from Italy and Slovenia, became public in February 2025 with the initial arrest of 13 people. Authorities dismantled an alleged criminal network that is accused of orchestrating the illegal import of hazardous waste from Germany, Italy, and Slovenia into Croatia.

title: A 900-Page Pre-Pantone Guide to Color from 1692: A Complete High-Resolution Digital Scan
content:
There’s ahead of its time, then there’s Traité des couleurs servant à la peinture à l’eau — or, in its original Dutch title, Klaer Lightende Spiegel der Verfkonst, a 900-page book of paint colors made before any such things were common tools of the artist’s, scientist’s, and industrial designer’s trade. Author and artist A. Boogert created one, and only one, copy of his extraordinary manual on color mixing in 1692. Appearing on the threshold of modern color theory, and featuring over 700 pages of color swatches, the book draws on Aristotle’s system of color rather than the new understanding of the color spectrum, fully elaborated by Newton in his Opticks over a decade later.

It would be another hundred years before a flood tide of color books began to make the theory more practical: from Goethe’s 1810 Theory of Colors and Werner’s 1814 Nomenclature of Colour to the dream of color standardization realized: the Pantone company, launched in 1963.

title: Von der Leyen pitches AI as solution to reduce reporting for European businesses
content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Monday pitched using artificial intelligence to streamline administrative procedures for European businesses as part of a broader push to simplify commerce and boost the EU’s competitiveness.

Speaking at a behind-closed-doors meeting of the European People’s Party in Taormina, Sicily, on Oct. 12, von der Leyen said the Commission would introduce an “only once” approach to business reporting. This would let companies submit information once, with AI helping public administrations use the data.

Von der Leyen argued that European companies repeatedly have to report the same information to public authorities, wasting time that businesses — and Europe — cannot afford, according to a copy of her speech seen by POLITICO.

“And this is why we will introduce ‘Only Once’, to report data only once – and with the help of AI the administration will ensure efficient use,” she said.

The speech marks the first time von der Leyen has explicitly pitched using AI specifically to reduce businesses’ administrative workload.

title: Donald Trump aligns with Vladimir Putin yet again, leaving Ukraine – and US relations with Europe – under pressure
content:
The deal struck by Donald Trump with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, on October 9 to allow Russia to sell millions of tonnes of diesel is a major departure from US policy and runs counter to Ukrainian and European interests. It also directly contradicts a law signed by the US president in September to authorise fresh US sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.

The timing of this deal was unfortunate. A senior Ukrainian and European delegation were in Miami for talks with Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. On the table were apparently new US proposals which included a pre-winter de-escalation in the four-and-a-half-year war.

Once in the room, the US envoys reportedly signalled that sanctions relief on Russia was coming. But this still left Ukrainian and European officials blindsided by the announcement. Unsurprisingly, the talks ended the same day without any agreement and a day earlier than planned.

title: Hooked on tuna: People have been harvesting these ocean predators for 44,000 years
content:
From a humble mayonnaise-laden sandwich to an expensive piece of sashimi, tuna is a prized source of food for people around the world. Once an inexpensive, easily shipped canned protein source, today’s bluefin tunas can fetch millions of dollars at auction. Millions of tons of tuna are harvested every year, supporting a global industry worth around US$40 billion annually.

But tunas are more than just the pink flesh found in cans and sushi, and humanity’s story with these fish goes back further than you might expect.

As a biologist and an archaeologist interested in long-term human-environment interactions, we wanted to investigate the deep record of people’s relationship with tunas.

title: Miksen ole vasemmistolainen?
content:
Oikeisto tekee nykyään kaikkensa, jotta minusta tulisi vasemmistolainen. Vasemmisto esittää usein hyviä tavoitteita, kun taas nykyoikeiston ajatuksia on välillä vaikea erottaa huonosta vitsistä. Mutta yritys ei onnistu. Olen edelleen ääriprogressiivinen sentristi.

Miksen sitten ole vasemmistolainen, vaikka jaan ison osan sen tavoitteista? Koska haluan, että ne toteutuvat. 

Minulla on maailmanparannukselle kaksi ehtoa: ratkaisuille pitää saada demokraattinen kannatus, ja niiden pitää toimia.

Jos ratkaisu edellyttää vasemmiston maailmanlaajuista vaalivoittoa, maailma jää pelastamatta.

Ilmastonmuutos ja luontokato eivät odota, että ihmiskunta omaksuu yhteisen maailmankuvan. Ratkaisujen pitää kelvata myös oikeistolaisille. Ei siksi, että he olisivat erityisen tärkeitä, vaan siksi, että heitäkin on olemassa.

Ei maailmaa pelasteta neljän vuoden aikana silloin tällöin. Pitää löytää ylipolitisoituneen pingpongin ja toistuvien vastareaktioiden sijaan malleja, jotka pysyvät vuosikymmeniä käytäntöinä.

title: Senegal: Brutal Crackdown Violates LGBT People’s Rights
content:
(Dakar) Senegal’s growing crackdown on Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender (LGBT) people is violating their rights, causing increasing fear and stigma, and should be ended immediately, Human Rights Watch said today. Mass arrests forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation appear to be part of an increase in punitive government action against LGBT people in West Africa.

On March 11, 2026, Senegal’s parliament amended article 319 of the penal code, doubling to 10 years the maximum prison term for consensual same-sex conduct and criminalizing “promotion” of or support to LGBT people and organizations. The amendment followed the detention by security forces of at least five men in Thiès region in December 2025 and 12 men in the capital, Dakar, in February 2026 on charges including “acts against nature” and “intentional transmission of HIV.” Police and gendarmerie then escalated arrests of suspected LGBT people in various other cities including Thiès, Rosso, Saint Louis, Yeumbeul, and Ziguinchor.

title: Entretien avec les artistes de Correspondance sous terre
content:
L’Institut finlandais et Ehkä Production ont invité l’artiste française Tilhenn Klapper et les artistes finlandaises Anna Torkkel et Ella Skoikka à participer à une correspondance créative de huit semaines au printemps 2025, alors que la nature commençait à fleurir et à germer. Le projet a été facilité et conceptualisé par l’artiste Saija Kangasniemi, productrice à l’Institut finlandais ce printemps.

À travers l’écriture d’un journal intime collectif, les artistes ont partagé leurs paysages intérieurs grâce à des écrits intuitifs quotidiens sur la vie ordinaire, extraordinaire et sur les choses souvent invisibles, ainsi que sur leurs pratiques artistiques liées à la danse et au son. L’artiste française Lia Pradal (Editions Païen) a conçu le livret imprimé du journal et réalisé les visuels du projet.

title: A Chinese Auto Giant Sponsors Portugal's National Football Team. Its Trucks Are Used by Russia to Attack Ukraine.
content:
As part of its “Vast Ocean Plan” for global expansion, one of China’s largest automotive companies recently announced its sponsorship of Portugal’s national football team.  

“Europe stands as a strategic priority,” Changan Automobile said in a press release in May, adding that its partnership with the Portuguese Football Federation offered a new opportunity for “brand engagement across the region.”

In an earlier phase of a global push by the state-owned company, Changan moved into Russia. Later, as international car makers left following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Changan started exporting more vehicles to fill the gap in the market, according to the industry analysis group inovev. 

Reporters found that some of those vehicles have been used in Russia's war against Ukraine, as launchpads for models of drones known to have attacked both military targets and civilians.

Changan Automobile did not respond to requests for comment. 

The Portugal Football Federation said the contract with Changan was signed after being reviewed for “the tight Federation compliance rules.”

title: How can Europe leverage laws to secure cloud sovereignty?
content:
European organizations have to reckon with how to keep up with the modern world without sacrificing sovereignty. Geopolitical instability, tightening regulatory expectations and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) mean that, for many organizations, sovereignty now sits alongside resilience and business continuity in board-level risk discussions. The question they can no longer defer is how to harness the opportunities of the modern cloud without surrendering control over their own data. Answering it requires honesty about what sovereignty means, and about where it can actually be found.

title: 300 glaciers have disappeared from the American West since the mid-20th century – the survivors have a few things in common
content:
From an airplane, most of the glaciers of the Rocky Mountain West look like small patches of white nestled into rugged landscape where the topography folds. The white is the snow cover, and lower down you can see the gray-blue bare ice.

In the middle of the 20th century, over 1,450 glaciers could be found in the contiguous U.S. Together, they covered 217 square miles (562 square kilometers) in six western states. Today, a comprehensive review my colleagues and I just published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences shows their total area has shrunk by 35% and they are still shrinking, perhaps faster.

A little more than 300 glaciers have disappeared, way more than I had anticipated.

Those that survive reflect just how vulnerable mountain glaciers have become as global temperatures rise. Where glaciers once covered large expanses of the western mountains thousands of years ago, most of the remaining glaciers in the Rockies and Sierra Nevada are small and found in topographically protected places.

title: Satavuotias arvotalo otti hukkalämmön hyötykäyttöön – lämmityskustannuksiin odotetaan 37 prosentin säästöä
content:
Helsingin Kalliossa, osoitteessa Suonionkatu 7, sijaitsevan arvokiinteistön lämmönjakohuoneessa kohtaavat historia ja tulevaisuus. Siellä, missä aikoinaan poltettiin hiiltä ja koksia, toimivat nykyään lämpöpumput, älykäs rakennusautomaatio ja poistoilman lämmöntalteenottojärjestelmä.

Arkkitehti Kaarlo Borgin suunnittelema, vuonna 1926 valmistunut rakennus on asemakaavalla suojeltu. Kiinteistöön kuuluu 64 asuntoa, seurakuntasiipi sekä katutason liiketiloja.

Helsingin seurakuntayhtymän tavoitteena oli löytää ratkaisu, joka vähentää energiankulutusta ja päästöjä, mutta säilyttää samalla rakennuksen historiallisen ilmeen.

– Tavoitteenamme oli ensisijaisesti pienentää kohteen hiilijalanjälkeä osana kirkon ilmastotavoitetta. Samalla halusimme leikata lämmityskustannuksia, sillä kaukolämmön hinta oli noin kymmenessä vuodessa tuplaantunut, Helsingin seurakuntayhtymän tilapalvelupäällikkö Pekka Suominen kertoo.

Ennen lämpö karkasi katolta – nyt se kierrätetään takaisin käyttöön

Kiinteistössä oli jo ennestään koneellinen poistoilmanvaihto, mikä mahdollisti lämmöntalteenoton toteuttamisen ilman laajoja ilmanvaihtojärjestelmän muutoksia.

title: Tutkijat: Pohjois-Euroopan vanhojen metsien tunnistamiseen tarvitaan yhteinen tieteellinen perusta
content:
Kansainvälinen tutkijaryhmä on julkaissut kokoavan katsauksen, jossa esitetään tieteeseen perustuvia kriteerejä Pohjois-Euroopan vanhojen metsien tunnistamiseen.

Julkaisu on tarkoitettu valtioiden rajat ylittäväksi tueksi päättäjille ja viranomaisille, jotka toteuttavat EU komission vaatimusta tunnistaa ja suojella jäljellä olevat vanhat ja luonnontilaiset metsät.

Vanhat metsät kuuluvat Euroopan arvokkaimpiin mutta samalla uhanalaisimpiin luonnonekosysteemeihin. Karkean arvion mukaan enää noin kolme prosenttia Euroopan metsistä täyttää luonnontilaisen tai vanhan metsän kriteerit. Niiden määrä vähenee edelleen myös Pohjois-Euroopassa.

Vanhojen metsien merkitys luonnon monimuotoisuudelle perustuu muun muassa metsien rakenteelliseen vaihteluun ja pitkän ajan kuluessa kehittyneisiin ekologisiin prosesseihin. Vanhat ja kuolleet puut sekä lahopuu tarjoavat elinympäristöjä esimerkiksi sienille, jäkälille, sammalille, lahopuusta riippuvaisille hyönteisille ja kolopesijöille.

title: UN: Burundi Set to Win Human Rights Council Seat Despite Abuses
content:
(New York) – Burundi is set to win re-election to the United Nations Human Rights Council in a vote on October 13, 2026, with no competition, Human Rights Watch said today. Burundi is seeking to retain its seat even though the government of this Central African country has not improved its abusive human rights conditions.

Burundi is one of the four African countries running for the same number of seats on the 47-nation council. The regional slates for the Western group, Latin America and the Caribbean, Central and Eastern Europe, and Asia also lack competition. This effectively guarantees all 15 candidates, fit or unfit, spots on the UN’s premier rights body for three years beginning on January 1, 2027. 

“This uncompetitive vote makes a mockery of the word ‘election,’” said Louis Charbonneau, UN director at Human Rights Watch. “UN member states should insist on competitive slates so they can reject candidates with poor human rights records. No one should have a seat on this crucial body handed to them on a silver platter.”

title: Fiji Criticized in U.S. Trafficking Report Over Failure to Tackle Grace Road Cult
content:
Fiji has been granted a one-year reprieve from a potential downgrade that could lead to U.S. aid cuts, amid concerns over its efforts to combat human trafficking, including its response to the Korean doomsday sect the Grace Road Group, according to a U.S. State Department report released last week.

This year’s Trafficking in Persons (TIP) report kept Fiji on its “Tier 2 Watchlist” of countries that do not fully meet the State Department’s minimum standards for combating human trafficking, noting that the Pacific island nation had failed to secure a trafficking conviction for three years running.

“Official complicity and corruption undermined anti-trafficking efforts and allowed traffickers to operate with impunity” in Fiji, the Oct. 8 report found.

However, the State Department granted Fiji a one-year waiver sparing it from being automatically downgraded to Tier 3, a designation that would have put it alongside countries including Iran and Afghanistan and could result in restrictions on U.S. non-humanitarian assistance.

Fiji, a country of just under a million people, has been on the Tier 2 Watchlist since 2024, but last year’s TIP report was the first to single out Grace Road.

title: How Europe plans to squeeze out Starlink
content:
BRUSSELS — Stepping on stage at the International Space Summit in Paris, French President Emmanuel Macron called on top European players to forge a new “alliance” to strengthen collective satellite capacity.

The real target of the let’s-team-up message? Elon Musk’s Starlink.

Macron’s speech last month was a public endorsement of a behind-the-scenes push that would see the bloc’s major telecoms companies make an aggressive play on direct-to-device connectivity — mobile signals beamed directly from satellites to phones.

On Tuesday, telecom ministers from EU national governments are gathering in Limerick, Ireland, to discuss a legislative proposal that could make it easier for top European carriers to get that satellite access.

The push would see Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone and Telefónica join forces to secure critical and coveted frequencies that will become available next year, as the European Commission eyes a new allocation procedure that would reserve frequencies for European players.

The plan, reported by Bloomberg ahead of Macron’s Sept. 10 speech, was confirmed to POLITICO by two people aware of the talks.

title: Economics Nobel: how this year’s winners helped to smooth the cycle of economic peaks and troughs
content:
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has awarded this year’s Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences to the American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford. The prize was awarded in recognition of their development of macroeconomic models that helped to reduce the length and depth of economic downturns.

According to the Academy, the economists’ work in macroeconomic modelling has given policymakers additional tools to smooth out the economic cycle. As well as reducing the severity of downturns, their work also helped to cool the potentially negative impacts of economic booms.

Economies are known to follow cycles of downturns and upturns – and economists have long sought to find ways to tame these. More than a century ago, British economist John Maynard Keynes developed an approach to managing the economy that came to be known as Keynesianism.

Before this, the classical “laissez-faire” approach dominated. According to this doctrine, in an economic downturn, markets would eventually clear and the economy would rebound. Any attempt by government to directly influence the economy would not work and could even make things worse.

title: Hungarian Ad Agency Got Millions From Firm Owned by Orban’s Billionaire Friend
content:
Just a few years after launching in 2020, Megafon Digital Incubator Center had become one of Hungary’s most influential political advertising agencies, mainly running social media campaigns in support of the ruling party and its leader, Viktor Orbán. 

But Megafon appears to have lost its sense of purpose since Orbán was swept from power in national elections this past April. Four months after that stunning loss, its website was taken offline.

Now, internal documents from a firm called V-Híd Zrt reveal the source of much of Megafon’s income. Around $12 million in donations came from that company, which is owned by Lőrinc Mészáros, Orbán’s childhood friend. 

Mészáros became fabulously wealthy during Orbán’s 16 years in power, building a business empire spanning sectors from construction to banking and energy. Mészáros’ companies won seven percent of all public procurement contracts — together worth about $2 billion — between 2018 and 2020 alone, according to Transparency International.

title: Snakebites are a far bigger problem than we knew: new study maps the hidden dangers
content:
Not every snakebite injects venom. When venom enters the body, however, it can cause snake envenoming. This is a potentially fatal condition and it mostly affects poor rural communities across tropical and subtropical regions who don’t have easy access to medical care.

As researchers with decades of combined experience in snakebite and tropical disease epidemiology, we came to realise that snake envenoming faces a data crisis. Over half of the countries where venomous snakes pose a threat don’t keep count of how many people are bitten or envenomed.

In rural sub-Saharan Africa and south Asia, many victims live hours away from the nearest clinic, lack transport, or seek care from traditional healers. As a result, their cases are never captured in national health statistics.

To bridge this massive gap, we conducted a study to map the global burden of snake envenoming and related deaths.

title: CIVICUS at the 89th Ordinary Session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
content:
The 89th session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights (ACHPR) will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 11 to 20 October, preceded by the NGO Forum, which will take place from 8 to 10 October.

The Forum on the Participation of NGOs provides an important platform for civil society organisations to share updates on the human rights situation across Africa and engage in collective advocacy ahead of the ACHPR session. The Forum will cover three main thematic areas: 

  • Status of human rights and democracy in Africa: Updates from sub-regional focal points on the general situation.
  • Special interest group discussions, which will allow participants to identify recommendations to address challenges raised in panel discussions.
  • Networking for human rights in Africa: Sharing experiences, best practices and lessons learnt towards durable solutions for forced displacement in Africa.

    • Under these themes, the Forum will deliberate on the following sub-themes: 

  • Water, sanitation, and the right to development
  • Civic space, governance, and democratic integrity
  • Natural resources, environmental justice, and climate-induced migration
  • Peace, security, and human rights

title: Trump misses out on Nobel Prize again and imposes new sanctions on the International Criminal Court. What does it mean?
content:
Rumours have been circulating for weeks about the United States imposing tougher sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), because of what US President Donald Trump sees as unfair targeting of Americans and Israelis for prosecution.

These sanctions finally came into effect on October 9 – the same day South African jurist Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her contribution to international law.

The motivations behind these two diametrically opposing moves speak to the fragility of international law. They also highlight that ICC member states – including Australia, Japan, EU states and Canada – might need to decide between Trump’s program to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick” and their own commitments to international justice.

The US has never been a strong supporter of the ICC. While it took part in negotiations that created the court’s founding treaty in 1998, it did so partly to ensure the crime of aggression remained off the court’s remit for decades.

Former President Bill Clinton did sign the Rome Statute in 1998, but it was never ratified. George W. Bush removed this possibility in 2002.

title: Scientists Detect Record-Breaking Radio Signal from the Ancient Universe
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that spotted a blast from the past, opened a portal between realms, yakked it up, and rose from the ashes.  

First, scientists have spotted a mysterious radio signal from the primordial universe that could illuminate cosmic evolution (it’s not aliens… sorry). Then: a diamond in the quantum rough, the decline of a fine bovine line, and a second-generation planet.  

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter The BeX Files. 

Caleb, Manisha et al. “A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang.” Science.

Scientists have discovered the most distant fast radio burst (FRB), a type of mysterious radio flare from space. This burst erupted when the universe was only three billion years old and sent radio waves across 10 billion light years before they reached Earth on March 4, 2024.

title: Taiwanin rooli Euroopan uudelleenteollistamisessa ja Suomen drooniteollisuudessa
content:
Kiinan tasavallan (Taiwanin) kansallispäivää vietetään 10. lokakuuta, ja se tarjoaa meille tilaisuuden tarkastella Taiwanin merkittävää kehitystä. Vuonna 1996 järjestettyjen ensimmäisten suorien presidentinvaalien jälkeen Taiwan on kehittynyt elinvoimaiseksi demokratiaksi, maailmanlaajuiseksi teknologiakeskukseksi ja maailman 20. suurimmaksi taloudeksi. Vaikka paine Manner-Kiinan ja Taiwanin välisissä suhteissa kasvaa, Taiwan on sitoutunut edistämään alueellista rauhaa, vakautta ja vaurautta.

Taiwan on kansainvälisen yhteisön korvaamaton jäsen, joka jakaa aktiivisesti kokemuksiaan ja asiantuntemustaan. Se muun muassa tuki kansanterveystoimia covid-19-pandemian aikana ja on vuodesta 2022 lähtien antanut Ukrainalle yli 130 miljoonalla eurolla taloudellista ja humanitaarista apua. Näin Taiwan on luonut Euroopan kanssa erityisen vahvan kumppanuuden, joka perustuu yhteisiin arvoihin ja taloudelliseen yhteistyöhön. Euroopasta on lisäksi viime vuosina tullut Taiwanin suurin ulkomaisten investointien lähde, mikä korostaa kahdenvälisten suhteidemme syvyyttä.

title: Gaza: Ceasefire Anniversary Marks Year of Failed Promises
content:
(Beirut) – Israeli forces continue to kill and wound civilians and deny sufficient food, aid, and water to Palestinians in Gaza one year after a ceasefire agreement took effect on October 10, 2025, Human Rights Watch said today. Israel’s acts of genocide and crimes against humanity, including forced displacement and extermination, have persisted throughout the ceasefire. Other countries should take immediate measures to protect civilians and ensure that rights-based reconstruction begins. 

The Board of Peace, authorized under United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803, is tasked with assessing parties’ compliance with the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. Promises of humanitarian relief and the restoration of essential civilian infrastructure are central to the plan. Yet, a year on, aid volumes remain far below required levels, critical humanitarian access routes have been repeatedly obstructed, and reconstruction has not yet begun. Continuing Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,400 Palestinians and wounded 4,881 others, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 2023 to over 74,000, including over 21,000 children.

title: As Trump’s Wall Closes in, DHS Intimidates a Border Tribe With Surveillance, Masked Agents and Drones
content:
At 4:59 a.m. on Aug. 25, Verlon Jose, the chairman of the Tohono O’odham Nation in Southern Arizona, received an email from the head of the U.S. Border Patrol’s Tucson Sector. Government contractors were en route to conduct soil tests for construction of a 62-mile wall along the Nation’s southern boundary, wrote acting chief patrol agent Henry N. Laxdal.

If the tribe wished to have cultural monitors observe the work, they were welcome to, but they could not interfere with the government’s operations.

The work would begin in exactly one minute.

Jose, 59, was already aware of the contractors’ arrival. An hour earlier, a tribal member had called to report a caravan heading south through the reservation, and Facebook was lighting up with similar accounts. The convoy included not only work trucks and drilling rigs, but Border Patrol vehicles as well.

title: Turkey bans social media for kids under 15
content:
The government of Turkey on Saturday formally banned access to social media platform for children under the age of 15.

The law was published today following the Turkish Parliament’s adoption of the bill last April. The ban will come into force on Nov. 1.

Social media platforms will have to “take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification,” to implement the new rules, the law states. The age verification system would work with a government-issued “token”, according to the law’s Article 7.

The law also includes provisions for minors over 15, stating that platforms cannot offer them services that could have “an addictive effect.”

Turkey has often implemented tough restrictions on social media services, frequently banning individual accounts from media outlets or activists, and at times banning access to entire platforms. Ankara banned Instagram for a week in 2024 amid claims the Meta-owned platform censored users mourning Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh.

Last week Turkey blocked a news website and its social media accounts over what a court deemed to be “LGBT propaganda,” sparking outrage from human rights and media freedom groups.

title: Watch: Inside Our $22K Sports Betting Experiment
content:
Earlier this year, we heard that reporter Jake Pearson planned to ask our editors at ProPublica for more than $20,000 so he could spend the NBA playoffs betting like a problem gambler. 

We told him we wanted in on the action. 

For 10 weeks, our documentary team at ProPublica filmed Jake as he dove ball-cap-first into DraftKings and FanDuel, the country’s largest online sportsbooks. Jake bet early, late and often, ramping up the amounts and frequency of his wagers, chasing his losses with even bigger bets.  He wanted to flagrantly wave the red flags of a gambler descending into addiction. Would the apps serve up speed bumps as he careened into the red, or would they push him to keep betting? 

Since 2018, the year the Supreme Court opened the door for states to legalize sports betting, the number of people staking money on games has exploded. It’s now legal in 39 states and Washington, D.C. The apps don’t just offer straight action on the outcome of a “Sunday Night Football” game — you can put money on myriad sports events and outcomes, including who will score the next point in a tense contest of Czech table tennis. Every month, millions do.

title: Factcheck: UK Conservatives double the ‘cost of net-zero’ after spreadsheet blunder
content:
A booklet published by the UK’s opposition Conservative party includes a “cost of net-zero” that appears to have been doubled by a spreadsheet error.

The “common sense” policy document argues that “what people ultimately want is a government competent enough to solve the problems for which it takes responsibility”.

In a section that says “sophisticat[ed]…modelling” should not be a substitute for “political judgement”, the “Right Way” document disparages various estimates of the cost of net-zero.

The Conservative document then claims – incorrectly – that the government’s official adviser, the Climate Change Committee (CCC), had put the cost of net-zero at close to £1tn. It says:

“In 2020, the CCC estimated that its route to net-zero would cost £957bn.”

In fact, the CCC’s 2020 estimate was exactly half this amount – £478bn – and last year it published a revised figure of £108bn, largely as a result of the falling cost of electric vehicles (EVs).

The Conservative party’s erroneous claim appears to stem from another report that had accidentally added up numbers twice, using a spreadsheet published by the CCC in 2020.

title: Reading For Change: Resources for Place-Based Systems Change
content:
The Place Project was a place-based systems change project in lutruwita/Tasmania. It was funded by the Paul Ramsay Foundation and the Tasmanian Community Fund and auspiced by Burnie Works. From 2024 it brought together people from Burnie, Devonport, kinimathatakinta/George Town, Brighton and Clarence Plains, as well as a multicultural place-based stream. The project wrapped up at the end of September 2026.

title: "Entire System of Cornell University Failed Her": Jane Doe Gang Rape Case Enrages Campus Community
content:
University students across the United States held a national day of action in solidarity with “Jane Doe,” the anonymous former student whose lawsuit alleging she was gang-raped by seven Cornell University Chi Phi fraternity members in 2024 has reignited outrage over how campuses and local law enforcement mishandle sexual assault cases and fail survivors. We go to Cornell’s campus in Ithaca, New York, where faculty have introduced a no-confidence resolution against the university administration.

“The number one message that Cornell students have is that Jane Doe’s ordeal is the tip of the iceberg, that there have been many, many other cases where women have been sexually assaulted and raped at Cornell University, and they’re afraid of coming forward. They’re afraid of going to the authorities because the investigation may be botched or they may be shamed,” says Paul Ortiz, a professor of labor history and the lead sponsor of the resolution.

title: Resisting the Menace of Federal Data Consolidation
content:
In the past two years, the federal government has unlawfully consolidated data exposing our private information. 

This consolidation has been chaotic but generally came in three rolling waves: It started with DOGE, moved to agency-to-agency data sharing with ICE, and then attempted data-driven purges of state voter rolls.

We all deserve to live in a world where the data we use to pay our taxes, receive benefits, and vote is not combined and weaponized against us. The amalgamation of data leads to mistakes, abuses, and a lack of trust in institutions meant to protect us. Overall, it can chill our participation in society. This is particularly true for groups disfavored by this administration—especially immigrants and protesters.

Congress highlighted similar abuses—including the creation of enemies lists and snooping on activists and federal employees—following the McCarthy and Watergate eras. And the increasing use of computers to magnify those harms led Congress to pass a slate of protections like the federal Privacy Act of 1974.

title: How to justify crimes against humanity: the Kremlin method

    • Pro-Kremlin FIMI campaigns promoted four narratives to justify Russia’s war against Ukraine: that Russia only strikes civilian infrastructure in retaliation; that recent attacks around Kyiv ended Moscow’s supposed restraint; that Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres are part of a “fight against Nazism” in Europe; and that NATO is preparing an offensive or blockade of Kaliningrad.

    These claims ignore extensive evidence of Russian attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, as well as documented war crimes. They also distort the chronology and the causes of the war. By blaming Ukraine, denying Russian wrongdoing, and weaponising heavily distorted Second World War narratives, pro-Kremlin actors seek to legitimise Russia’s aggression and portray Moscow as the victim and protector of Europe.

title: Climate disinformation: new report confirms that political will is there, but actions remain limited at national level
content:
A new report from the Forum on Information and Democracy (FID) finds notable political will and promising efforts to strengthen information integrity on climate change in at least 23 countries and the EU. However, it also finds persistent gaps, such as lack of national strategic plans of action to tackle climate disinformation and greenwashing from the fossil fuel lobby, which is most urgently needed.

As the world prepares for COP 17 on Biodiversity (22-30 October) and COP31 on climate change (9-22 November), the findings pave the way for policymakers and regulators to take the urgent action needed to tackle climate disinformation. 

Covering 23 countries and the EU, the report was developed within the framework of the organization’s priority workstream on Information Integrity on Climate and the Environment, co-chaired by Armenia and Brazil.  It shows that while political traction and public awareness are rising, most countries still don’t have a national strategic plan of action to counter climate disinformation and denialism.

“The Trump administration has made clear its aim to destroy the ICC to shield US and Israeli officials from facing charges before the court,” said Philippe Bolopion, executive director of Human Rights Watch. “By attacking the court, the US government is threatening justice for victims of abuses from Palestine to Ukraine, Myanmar, and Sudan.”

title: Teiden varsilla sijaitsevat taimitarhat palvelevat viilennystä kaipaavia daressalaamilaisia – Yrittäjille bisnes on epävarmaa
content:
Riveittäin kukkia, pensaita, nuoria puita ja taimia reunustaa tietä vilkkaassa Mbezi Louisin kaupunginosassa Dar es Salaamissa. Osa kasveista on pakattu pieniin muovipusseihin tai kierrätettyihin vesipulloihin, jotkut ovat jo niin isoja, että ne varjostavat pienempiä kasveja.

David Simon, joka tunnetaan paremmin Ngoshana, kävelee kasvien välissä, tarkistaa niiden kuntoa ja puhuu asiakkaiden kanssa. Muutaman metrin päässä surisee busseja, moottoripyöriä ja autoja.

Ngoshan taimitarha sijaistee lähellä Dar es Salaamiin johtavaa moottoritietä. Hänelle tienvierusta on sekä työpaikka että näyteikkuna. Liiketila on vain lainassa, ja sen ympärillä oleva kaupunki muuttuu jatkuvasti.

”Jotkut ohikulkijat saattavat huomata kasvin ja kysyä hintaa mennessään töihin mutta eivät palaa ostamaan sitä paluumatkalla. Jos kasvi viehättää heitä, joskus he maksavat siitä ja pyytävät minua säilyttämään sitä puolestaan”, hän kertoo.

title: We Are Already Post-Human
content:
From Silicon Valley to the Vatican, across kitchen tables and in the halls of power, the world is astir over the question of whether humans will be able to control the AIs we’ve created. But that begs the question: What does it mean to be “human”?

One place to start sorting this all out is what Confucian philosophy calls “rectification” — naming things for what they actually are.

To N. Katherine Hayles, author of “Bacteria to AI: Human Futures with our Non-human Symbionts,” we are already “post-human.”

As she explained to Claire Webb in a recent Futurology podcast, the concept of “human” is culturally and historically contingent. These days, she says, there is still the dominant view that arose with the Enlightenment of the human as an autonomous, singular entity with “rational free will.”

For Hayles, that has never been true because humans have never existed as an entity apart but have always been “woven in the web” of a surrounding environment, or “Umwelt.” It is the symbiotic interactions within that interdependence which determine the signs we sense, the meaningful interpretation of the information we process, the decisions we make, and the actions we take that define who we are.

title: Montenegro Arrests then Expels Russian 'Rybar' Network Leader, Associates
content:
Montenegrin authorities detained on Friday five persons believed to be the leaders of the Russian media and influence network "Rybar," which Western security agencies view as a sophisticated tool for Kremlin influence operations.

Prime Minister Milojko Spajić framed the action in a post on X as a national security and foreign interference operation.

Spajić noted his government had previously warned of "attempts at hybrid action and destabilization of Montenegro" as the nation pursues European Union integration. Cautioning against "hasty statements," the Prime Minister stated that "serious indications" require every lead to be thoroughly investigated within a broader security context.

"Institutions are doing their job, Montenegro is protecting its interests, and no one will endanger our European future," Spajić wrote.

Montenegrin daily Vijesti cited the Montenegrin Police Directorate as stating the arrests were carried out with the support of "international partners" in order to neutralize illegal activities.

title: David Byrne’s New Book Explores the Strange Afterlife of Good Ideas: From Vermeer’s Paintings to Roman Concrete & Dark Matter
content: David Byrne will always be most widely known as the co-founder and frontman of Talking Heads. That may count among the greatest possible achievements for any artist — to the minds of many an Open Culture reader, at least — but it must occasionally frustrate the man himself. Talking Heads broke up 35 years ago, but Byrne has only grown more and more productive since, recording his own albums, creating musicals, writing books, putting on PowerPoint presentations, and even designing bike racks. By now, his ideas have stretched so far beyond music that he’s considering the nature of ideas themselves, how they succeed or fail in catching on, and why they go in and out of acceptance over time. Hence his new book Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up.

title: Miten yhtenäinen Iso-Britannia on?
content:
Ulkoapäin voi näyttää siltä, että Britannia on yksi yhtenäinen maa, jota johtaa pääministeri Lontoosta. Todellisuudessa saarivaltion eri puolilla haaveillaan itsenäisyydestä.

Maanantaina 14.9.2026 Skotlannin, Walesin ja Pohjois-Irlannin johtajat allekirjoittivat yhteistyösopimuksen, jossa muun muassa todettiin, että Westminsterin, eli Yhdistyneen kuningaskunnan keskushallinnon aika on ohi. Johtajat vaativat perustuslaillisia muutoksia, jotta maat saisivat enemmän valtaa päättää omista asioistaan. Heidän mukaansa keskushallinnon ei pitäisi rajoittaa maiden oikeutta järjestää kansanäänestys itsenäistymisestä.

Yhdistynyt kuningaskunta (eli Britannia) on suvereeni valtio, johon kuuluu neljä maata: Englanti, Wales, Skotlanti ja Pohjois-Irlanti. Englanti on näistä maista selvästi suurin niin väkiluvultaan kuin bruttokansantuotteeltaan: Englannin osuus koko Britannian bruttokansantuotteesta on yli 85 prosenttia, ja noin 85 prosenttia Britannian väestöstä asuu Englannissa.

title: New York Plans Stronger Sports Betting Regulation to Curb Gambling Addiction
content:
Gambling regulators in New York on Friday formally proposed two rules that they say will help curb gambling addiction in the state.

The move adds the country’s largest sports betting market to a growing list of places that are seeking online gambling reforms as states that have legalized wagering on sports in recent years deal with the harmful side effects, including rising addiction diagnoses there.

While the drafts have been months in the making, their official introduction follows mounting media scrutiny, including a ProPublica investigation last month that showed weaknesses in the guardrails that companies like DraftKings have erected to address problem gamblers on their platforms. That system is called “responsible gaming.”

The commission’s chair, Brian O’Dwyer, said that the proposed rules “provide an opportunity for the industry to illustrate its commitment” to protecting its customers. 

“The industry is on notice by me and this commission that they need to solve this problem,” O’Dwyer said. “If the industry does not address it, then we will address it and they may not like the solution that we come up with.”

content:

Nämä tarinat julkaistaan äänipodcastina, kaikkien kuunneltavaksi verkkoon. title: Markku Tannerin muistoseminaarissa katsottiin rohkeasti tulevaan
content:
Kotiseutuliiton pitkäaikaisen toiminnanjohtajan Markku Tannerin elämäntyötä kunnioitettiin 8. lokakuuta Helsingissä Karjalatalolla järjestetyssä muistoseminaarissa. Lämminhenkisessä tilaisuudessa muisteltiin Tannerin mittavia ansioita suomalaisen kotiseututyön hyväksi, mutta samalla suunnattiin katse tulevaisuuteen: kotiseututyö nähtiin ennen kaikkea yhteisöjen, luottamuksen ja turvallisuuden rakentamisena.

Tilaisuuteen kokoontui monikymmenpäinen joukko Tannerin perheenjäseniä, ystäviä, työtovereita, kotiseututoimijoita, yhteistyökumppaneita sekä hänen työnsä jatkajia. Muistoseminaarin puheenvuorot luotasivat Tannerin elämäntyötä kolmesta näkökulmasta: karjalaisuus, kaupunkilaisuus ja yhteisöllisyys. Esiin nousivat sekä Tannerin poikkeuksellinen työura että hänen merkittävä vaikutuksensa suomalaisen kotiseututyön kehittämiseen. Tilaisuudessa kuultiin niin läheisten, tutkijoiden, nuorten toimijoiden kuin eri järjestöjenkin edustajien näkemyksiä hänen elämäntyöstään.

title: Ny skiva med flöjtensemblen Tuultenpesä förenar musik, minnen och kulturarv
content:
Hemvist är den finsk-svenska flöjtsextetten Tuultenpesäs andra album. Skivans tema kretsar kring frågor om tillhörighet, migration, minne och identitet. Skivan ges ut i samarbete med Finlands svenska folkmusikinstitut.

Tuultenpesäs karakteristiska ljudvärld formas av ett rikt urval flöjter från olika tider och traditioner. Åspipor, Härjedalspipor, Månmarkapipor, honkahuilu-flöjter, blockflöjter och tvärflöjter möter Leena Laitinens sång i musik som rör sig mellan stillhet och rytmisk energi, mellan enkelhet och flerstämmiga klanglandskap.

Materialet på skivan bygger på äldre uppteckningar och arkivinspelningar av finlandssvensk folkmusik. Traditionella melodier och visor från bland annat Oravais, Purmo, Petalax, Korsnäs, Sibbo, Borgå och Mörskom vävs samman med svensk folkmusik och ensemblemedlemmarnas egna kompositioner.

Tuultenpesä grundades 2016 och består av Kristiina Ilmonen, Mimmi Laaksonen, Leena Laitinen, Göran Månsson, Kirsi Ojala och Jonas Simonson. Debutalbumet Vindstilla utkom 2022.

Hemvist publiceras digitalt på bland annat Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, Deezer och Pandora samt ges ut på cd. Läs texthäftet här.

title: Save the date och anmäl din programpunkt till Vårmötet 2027
content:
Oväntade och väntade samarbeten som utvecklar museerna och samhället

Museerna har med sin kunskap, sina många kompetenser och sitt höga förtroende en stark position i samhället. Men i en värld som förändras snabbt behöver också museerna utvecklas, öppna för nya perspektiv och hitta nya lösningar tillsammans med andra.

Under Museernas vårmöte i Gävle den 27–29 april 2027 utforskar vi vad som blir möjligt i mötet med andra. Hur kan samarbeten inom museibranschen och med forskning, näringsliv, civilsamhälle, skola, tech, kreativa näringar och offentliga aktörer bidra till innovation, nya publiker och större samhällsnytta? Och hur kan vi samtidigt värna museernas oberoende och trovärdighet?

Genom erfarenheter, goda exempel och nya perspektiv undersöker vi hur mötet med andra kan göra museerna starkare, öppnare och bättre rustade för framtiden.

Var med och bidra med dina erfarenheter och reflektioner! Vi välkomnar programförslag som vill utforska årets tema från olika perspektiv, från olika professioners vardag och som visar på vägen framåt i sektorn. Ta gärna med era samarbetspartners!

title: The best sunrise alarm clocks in the UK, tried and tested for gentler mornings
content:
Our reviewer sheds some light on the best dawn simulation alarms, from Lumie and Philips to Dreamegg

• The best eye masks to help you sleep better

To wake each day in darkness is a plight you wouldn’t wish on your worst enemy, yet that’s what many of us do routinely throughout winter. Getting up in the dark decouples our life from our circadian rhythm (our body clock), with bodily processes such as cognition and metabolism put to work before they’re fully prepped.

Thank heavens, then, for sunrise alarm clocks. These “dawn simulation” devices glow with gradually intensifying brightness as your wake-up time approaches, kickstarting your circadian rhythm before you get out of bed. For many users, this results in a happier, healthier start to the day.

title: Lausunto luonnoksesta hallituksen esitykseksi eduskunnalle laiksi tekijänoikeuslain muuttamisesta
content:
VN/34805/2025

Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriölle

Musiikin luovan alkutuotannon toimijat kiittävät mahdollisuudesta lausua luonnoksesta hallituksen esitykseksi tekijänoikeuslain muuttamisesta. Musiikin luova alkutuotanto kokoaa yhteen Teoston ja sen jäsenjärjestöt: Suomen Musiikintekijät, Suomen Säveltäjät ja Suomen Musiikkikustantajat.

Musiikin tekijöiden ja kustantajien näkökulmasta tekijänoikeuksien tehokas suoja, toimivat lisensointijärjestelmät ja oikeudenhaltijoiden mahdollisuus valvoa oikeuksiaan ovat keskeisiä edellytyksiä ammattimaiselle luovalle työlle. Pidämme esitettyjä muutoksia pääosin perusteltuina ja kannatettavina.

  • Pidämme perusteltuna tekijänoikeuslain 11 §:n 5 momenttiin esitettyä selvennystä tilapäisestä kappaleen valmistamisesta.
  • Kannatamme tekijänoikeuslain 60 a §:n uudistamista vastaamaan EU:n täytäntöönpanodirektiivin 8 artiklan vaatimuksia.
  • Esitämme, että tekijänoikeuslain 60 a §:ään lisätään uusi momentti, jossa huomioidaan NIS2-direktiivin ja sähköisen viestinnän palveluista annetun lain mukaiset verkkotunnusten rekisteröinti- ja haltijatietojen luovuttamista koskevat vaatimukset.

title: Women are more emotionally intelligent than men, and that’s a problem – landmark study
content:
Who comes to mind when you think of someone emotionally intelligent? Someone who can read a room, defuse an argument, and who knows exactly what to say when a friend is struggling? For many people, that person is a woman. It’s such a widely held belief that popular psychology treats it as fact.

We decided to put that assumption to the test. Our new study, co-led by Dr Vera Hampel and co-authored with Leon Bach, reviewed nearly three decades of research, from 1995 to 2023, across 76 countries and more than 600,000 people. We wanted to answer a simple question: are women really more emotionally intelligent than men? The headline answer is yes, on average, women score higher.

But the more useful finding is the type of emotional intelligence women seem to excel at, and what it potentially costs the people who have it.

Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognise, understand and regulate emotions in yourself and in others. When we looked at each element of emotional intelligence, the female advantage turned out to be concentrated in the “others’ feelings” half of the equation.

title: Vuoden 2026 nuori kliininen tutkija Markus Haapanen: ”Tutkimuksista puuttuvat usein lääkkeitä eniten käyttävät, eli hauraat ja monisairaat ikääntyneet”
content:
Vuoden nuoreksi kliiniseksi tutkijaksi valittu Markus Haapanen on rakentanut vahvan kansainvälisen verkoston, ja hän on julkaissut laajasti geriatrian alan johtavissa kansainvälisissä tiedelehdissä. Lääketeollisuus pitää tutkimustyötä ja siihen kannustamista tärkeänä, sillä vaikuttava tutkimus tuottaa vaikuttavia hoitoja.

Haapanen toimii apulaisprofessorina kliinisen lääketieteen tutkimusyksikössä Oulun yliopistossa, vanhempana tutkijana Folkhälsanin tutkimuskeskuksessa sekä geriatriaan erikoistuvana lääkärinä Vantaa-Keravan hyvinvointialueen kotiin vietävissä lääkäripalveluissa.

”Tuoreena implementaatiolääketieteen professorina Markus Haapanen on tuonut näkyvästi esiin kliinisen tutkimuksen merkitystä niin lääkärikunnan, nuorten tutkijoiden kuin suuren yleisön keskuudessa. Hän on myös edistänyt tutkimuksen arvostusta toimimalla aktiivisena mentorina, tutkijakouluttajana ja esikuvana”, sanoo palkintolautakunnassa toimiva Nuorten Lääkärien Yhdistyksen puheenjohtaja Markus Hautamäki.

Valtiovarainministeriö ei yllättänyt ketään korostamalla velkajarrun toteuttamisen välttämättömyyttä tämän viikon virkapuheenvuorossa. Yllätys ei ollut myöskään ministeriön vakuutus, että hyvinvointiyhteiskunta kyllä kestää lisää sopeutuksia.

Velkaantumisen pysäyttäminen on tarpeen, eikä hyvinvointiyhteiskuntaa voi rahoittaa velalla loputtomiin. Olennaista on, miten sopeutus tehdään: mitä tehdään, paljonko, mistä ja millä seurauksilla.

VM vaatii, että kaikki menot ja tulot otetaan tarkasteluun. Vaatimus on oikea, ja siitä seuraa, ettei yksikään puolue voi pitää pyhiä lehmiään koskemattomina. Myös puolustusmenojen kasvua, maataloustukia ja eläkkeitä on voitava arvioida kriittisesti, vaikka se olisi poliittisesti hankalaa.

Kokoomus on ilmoittanut sopeuttavansa pelkillä leikkauksilla. Ajatukselle ei näy tukea muilta puolueilta tai talousoppineilta, ja myös VM on viestittänyt, ettei ilman veronkorotuksia selvitä. Kun vaatimus on, että kaikki keinot katsotaan, se koskee myös verotusta.

title: Ylioppilaslehden Ideakilpailun finalistit on valittu
content:
”No kyllä täältä kelpaa tuomaroida”, todettiin, kun Ylioppilaslehden ideakilpailun tuomaristo eli Esa Mäkinen, Vappu Kaarenoja, Antti Pikkanen ja Veikko Eranti kokoontui Sanomatalon ylimmän kerroksen kokoushuoneeseen aurinkoisena keskiviikkoiltapäivänä. Edessä oli tärkeä tehtävä: valita kilpailutöiden joukosta ne ehdotukset, jotka kutsutaan finaaliin tavoittelemaan 1 000 euron pääpalkintoa.

Tunnelma oli odotettavissa olevista vaikeista päätöksistä huolimatta hyvä. Ideakilpailu on ensimmäinen laatuaan, eikä kukaan rehellisesti ottaen täysin tiennyt, mitä siltä odottaa. Siksi tuomareita ilahduttivat ehdotusten määrä ja korkea taso sekä se, kuinka samoja haasteita lähestyttiin hyvin erilaisista näkökulmista.

Kilpailutöissä nousi esiin erityisesti opiskelijoiden ja Ylioppilaslehden välinen suhde. Monissa ehdotuksissa pohdittiin, miten yhteisöllisyyttä voitaisiin vahvistaa ja miten lehti voisi tulla lähemmäs opiskelijoiden arkea. Ehdotuksissa käsiteltiin myös uusia kumppanuusmalleja, yhteisöjournalismia, monimediaalisia sisältöjä sekä muuttuvia mediankäyttötapoja ja opiskelijoiden informaatiokuormaa.

title: Navi Pillay, South African Jurist, Wins Nobel Peace Prize in "Stinging Rebuke to Donald Trump"
content:
The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay’s long career in international human rights law includes work as a defense attorney for anti-apartheid activists, president of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, a former judge at the International Criminal Court and the U.N.’s high commissioner for human rights from 2008 to 2014.

“Everybody in the human rights movement reveres Navi Pillay,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, who calls the award “a stinging rebuke to Donald Trump.” Brody, a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua, also comments on the Trump administration’s decision to deport a Nicaraguan opposition activist, Jeffrey Jarquín, from the United States, where he was in the process of seeking asylum. Upon his return to Nicaragua, Jarquín was immediately imprisoned at the same facility in which he was once tortured.

title: Organizing in the Town at Oakland Tech Week
content:
EFF was thrilled to join organizers, advocates, and activists in the East Bay for the second annual Oakland Tech Week last week. We are grateful to our friends at MediaJustice and Upturn for inviting us co-present this all-day event, “Building Beyond Big Tech: Organizing Oakland’s Future”, on Sept. 30.  The event, hosted by the Kapor Center in downtown Oakland, offered a unique chance to spend time with people across The Town and the Bay Area working to create a better future for everyone.

“We’re at this truly consequential moment,” said EFF executive director Nicole Ozer, in her speech kicking off the day’s events. “We know that in this community’s work—and communities across the country—our ability to ensure that technology empowers rather than oppresses is fundamental to the future of countries, our livelihoods, and, literally, our lives.”

title: Subsea cables and oil pipelines: The infrastructure linking AI, empire, and occupation
content:
Internet infrastructure policy is increasingly a topic of discussion in military strategy and policy decision-making

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot of the Internet Infrastructure Map in 2026, from kmcd.dev. Fair use

By Alli Armijo

This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.

The internet has always been illusive. Stretching bodies of water, screens, and time zones, it exists in a plurality increasingly shaped by big tech. And the cables mediate this; the cables are its nervous system.

With over 600 active and planned underwater internet cables spanning over 1.5 million kilometers around the globe, the majority of subsea infrastructure is predominantly owned and operated by US tech monopolies, namely Google, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft. 

This infrastructure is largely laid on trans-Atlantic slave ship and oil extraction routes, algorithmically bound by a legacy of colonial violence and exploitative labor practices.

title: War’s Hidden Mental Health Toll on Children with Disabilities
content:
As armed conflicts proliferate around the globe, World Mental Health Day is a reminder that the psychological toll stemming from hostilities result in mental health harms that have lasting effects on people’s lives. Insecurity, trauma, anxiety, and confusion are the norm for many who have endured armed conflict.

Access to services is frequently inadequate—even though over a fifth of conflict-affected populations are estimated to experience mental health conditions such as post-traumatic stress, depression or anxiety. For people, including children, with intellectual disabilities, these harms can be compounded by social, attitudinal, and environmental barriers, which interact with their disability and can heighten their exposure to violence and exclusion.

title: Kidnappings and Home Invasions Soar as French Syndicates Extort Crypto
content:
A father beaten and forced into a car trunk. A magistrate and her mother held hostage for 30 hours. A family terrorized overnight in northern France for digital cash. Over the past two years, a violent wave of kidnappings and home invasions has swept across France targeting cryptocurrency executives, influencers, and their loved ones, as criminal networks increasingly turn to physical torture to extort digital fortunes.

Organized criminal networks increasingly turn to home invasions, physical torture, and abductions to extort digital fortunes. Authorities have recorded 77 such incidents so far this year, up from 67 in 2025 and roughly 20 in 2024, according to data from France’s National Prosecutor’s Office for Organized Crime, known as PNACO.

While the early wave of violence primarily targeted high-profile industry executives and wealthy influencers, law enforcement officials warn that criminal syndicates are increasingly hunting ordinary citizens suspected of holding digital wallets. Just weeks ago, four armed intruders held a family captive overnight in the northern town of Vendin-le-Vieil, forcing the father to hand over about 40,000 euros, or $47,000, in cryptocurrency.

title: The Pentagon Gave $350 Million in Contracts to a Firm Closely Tied to a Senior Defense Department Official
content:
Among a cadre of Wall Street executives brought into the Pentagon during President Donald Trump’s second term, George K. Kollitides II has emerged as a powerbroker with a broad mandate to improve procurement of weapons and critical minerals.

The longtime partner at the private equity firm Alvarez & Marsal Capital has framed his tour of duty in government as a service to the country. But the work he’s leading has also been a boon to his old friends in the private sector, government procurement records show.

In April, months after Kollitides had started work at the Pentagon, he was listed on a securities filing as continuing to work for his old company as a senior adviser. Two months later, the Defense Department finalized a $281 million no-bid consulting contract with an affiliate firm, Alvarez & Marsal Federal, to advise Kollitides’ new Pentagon office, the records show.

title: End of Abyss review – a creepy dollhouse take on Resident Evil and The Thing
content:
PlayStation 5 (version played), Xbox, PC; Epic Games Publishing
This fetchingly presented horror game brings style and scares, but overextends itself with repetition

A small band of soldiers enters an abandoned facility, where puckered flesh sprouts from cold steel. It’s a promising but familiar start to a sci-fi horror story, with heavy overtones of Alien and The Thing. Neither of those, though, were so … dinky.

End of Abyss’s facility is presented as a kind of a model-village recreation of The Thing’s Outpost 31 that you peer into from above. Your little bobble-headed hero takes up a tiny fraction of the screen, with most of the remainder drenched in foggy darkness, or even blanked out entirely. This is a world of Usborne-style cutaways, where anything outside the walls is total blackness.

title: Peruskoulun voima on sen hitaudessa
content:
Peruskoulussa opetetaan perustietoja ja -taitoja, jotka muuttuvat hitaasti, vaikka tieteenalat kehittyvät. Esimerkiksi matematiikan opiskelu on jatkossakin luontevaa aloittaa peruslaskutoimituksista, vaikka matematiikka tieteen alana kehittyy koko ajan.

Koulutusjärjestelmämme pohjaa ajatukseen, että sen huipulla on alansa uusimpaan ja parhaimpaan tietoon pohjautuva korkeakoulutus. Tasapainoilu alkuopetuksen liikkumattoman lähtöpisteen ja alati kauemmas karkaavan korkeakoulutuksen välillä on tuttua peruskoulun ylemmillä luokilla ja toisen asteen opinnoissa. Missään kohdassa ei saisi tulla liian isoa loikkaa, jotta kukin ikäluokka pysyy opinnoissa mukana. 

Toisaalta pitäisi huolehtia, että peruskoululaiset ovat valmiita siirtymään toisen asteen ammatillisiin tai lukio-opintoihin, ja toisaalta siitä, että toisen asteen opinnot antavat riittävät valmiudet korkeakouluun. Tämän yhtälön pyörittäminen on osa koulutus- ja tiedeyhteisön perusarkea ja rullaa omalla painollaan. Opetussuunnitelmia tehdään ja oppimateriaaleja päivitetään.

title: "Abolish ICE": Protests Erupt in NYC After ICE Agents Shoot Father with 5-Year-Old Son in Car
content:
Protests have erupted in New York City after a federal immigration agent shot and wounded a man in the Bronx on Thursday afternoon. As masked agents reportedly posing as construction workers attempted to arrest 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, they opened fire on his car. Belgal was shot in the neck. His 5-year-old child, who was in the back seat, was physically unharmed. Belgal was taken to a local hospital, where hundreds, including our guests, Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York City Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa, gathered to demand his release.

“What we saw yesterday was a prime example of why [ICE] is a terror to our communities, why it should not exist,” says Avila Chevalier. She was among multiple people assaulted by officers with the NYPD unit that specializes in protest policing, known as the Strategic Response Group (SRG). Four others were arrested at Thursday evening’s protest. Avila Chevalier, who was knocked down to the ground by officers, says, “This is why we also must demand that we get rid of and disband the SRG, because this type of response should have never happened for folks who were just simply trying to protect their neighbor.”

title: Turkish Crackdown On LGBTQ+ Organizations Threatens Freedom of Expression and Association
content:
EFF strongly condemns Turkey’s state-led discriminatory, oppressive attacks on feminist and LGBTQ+ organisations, media platforms, student groups, and rights defenders and activists within the country.

Since mid-September, access to the websites and social media accounts of a dozen organizations have been blocked by court order, while over 60 members and activists have been detained, their offices and homes raided, mobile phones, laptops and other digital devices seized, and judicial proceedings launched against them. 

These actions threaten the very existence of the LGBTQ+ organizations targeted, limiting their ability to carry out legitimate human rights work, deterring participation and support, and chilling the free speech rights of not just these groups, but any organization that even reports on LGBTQ+ oppression.

A little over a week ago, an Istanbul court shut down the website and social media accounts of T24, Turkey’s longest running independent digital news organization—which has covered government-backed campaigns against and earlier crackdowns on gay rights groups—alleging it had aired “LGBT propaganda” over the past year.

title: Lithuanian Minister Condemns Intimidation Campaign against Investigative Reporters
content:
Lithuanian Culture Minister Lukas Alsys condemned the harassment of journalists and editors on Thursday after being asked about growing pressure on 15min staff following the news outlet’s joint investigation with OCCRP into the crypto-finance firm Bankera.

“Any persecution of journalists or editors aimed at intimidating or frightening them is completely intolerable,” Alsys told Žinių Radijas, adding that relevant authorities should “draw conclusions.”

The joint investigation revealed that more than 45 million euros raised during Bankera’s 2017–2018 token sale was transferred to Pacific Private Bank in Vanuatu, an offshore entity acquired by Bankera’s three co-founders. Records showed the bank subsequently issued millions of euros in loans to the founders and their companies, including funds used to purchase luxury real estate.

Lithuania’s Financial Crime Investigation Service opened a pre-trial investigation shortly after the story was published in April 2025. Vanuatu’s central bank later revoked Pacific Private Bank’s international license, though the decision was stayed pending appeal.

What followed was a systematic campaign of pressure targeting journalists and executives at 15min.

title: Ken Paxton’s Security for Travel Cost Taxpayers Millions. Just 1 in 6 of His Trips Had a Stated Business Purpose.
content:
In the summer of 2023, after he was impeached on charges of abusing his office for personal gain, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was suspended and barred from conducting any official business for more than three months while awaiting trial in the state Senate.

So, he traveled.

Paxton, a Republican who is now running for U.S. Senate, took at least 17 trips over three months, including to resort destinations Park City, Utah, and Vail, Colorado. He visited the Oklahoma town where he owns a vacation lodge and a Utah community with a golf resort, where he later bought four condominiums.

State police joined him each time, costing taxpayers tens of thousands of dollars for trips unrelated to his job as attorney general. The Texas Senate ultimately acquitted him on the impeachment charges.

But Paxton’s use of the taxpayer-funded detail did not begin or end there. In fact, it stands out compared with his predecessor, fellow elected officials in Texas and other state attorneys general, ProPublica and The Texas Tribune found.

title: Arvot vaikuttavat siihen, ostetaanko kunnostettua elektroniikkaa
content:
Kuluttajien käsitykset uudelleenvalmistetuista elektroniikkatuotteista perustuvat usein enemmän tunteisiin kuin tietoon niiden todellisista ominaisuuksista. Siksi käytettyihin ja sittemmin kunnostettuihin tuotteisiin liitettyjä mielikuvia tulisi muokata eri kuluttajaryhmille sopiviksi.

title: IKEA Stopped Selling in Russia. But its Former Belarusian Supplier Filled the Gap — With Strikingly Similar Furniture
content:
When the Swedish furniture giant IKEA exited Russia and Belarus in 2022 in response to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it instructed its suppliers to do the same. A Lithuanian supplier complied, and stopped sourcing IKEA products from its Belarusian factory.

But the Belarusian factory didn’t stop exporting furniture after losing the rights to IKEA designs. Instead, it appears to have filled an IKEA-shaped void in the Russian market, exporting pieces that are strikingly similar to the Swedish designs.

The website of one Russian retailer even told customers that “IKEA's departure doesn't mean you have to give up your familiar interior design style,” adding that they “now have the opportunity to buy those same beloved products.”

“Yes, their appearance and names have changed slightly,” the blurb on the website said. “But the design, quality, ease of purchase, and ease of assembly remain unchanged.”

IKEA said it could not comment on individual cases, but noted that it “continuously monitors potential infringements” on its intellectual property rights.

title: An Arizona County’s “Housing Hub” Is a Dead End for Many Homeless Families
content:
A decade ago, nonprofit leaders in Arizona’s most populous county boasted that they had created the Amazon of homeless service systems. Families in crisis would no longer have to contact a dozen agencies in search of shelter or housing. A single system could point them to help.

But for all the hype, this system has become a dead end for many families. A 2023 evaluation found 94% of people who were assessed for housing help by the system didn’t receive it. And that didn’t account for parents who were unable to connect with a worker to see if they qualified for assistance.

Families say it hasn’t improved.

In interviews, 30 families that are homeless told ProPublica that calling the hotline, meeting with outreach workers or showing up at shelters rarely results in offers of help. Some families said they called 211 multiple times without being connected to the homeless response system for families, known as the Family Housing Hub. Others, who said they were sleeping in cars or outdoors, said they couldn’t get a spot on the waitlist for shelter.

title: Värdena påverkar om renoverad elektronik köps
content:
Konsumenters uppfattningar om återuppbyggda elektroniska produkter baseras ofta mer på känslor än på kunskap om deras faktiska egenskaper. Därför bör bilderna som är kopplade till begagnade och senare renoverade produkter modifieras för att passa olika konsumentgrupper.

SuFiRe-projektet, koordinerat av Åbo yrkeshögskola, undersökte affärsstudenters attityder till ombyggda elektroniska produkter. Totalt deltog 270 studenter från Finland, Sverige och Ungern i studien.

Återuppbyggda elektroniska produkter, det vill säga elektroniska produkter som har samlats in och renoverats vid användning, blir allt vanligare som en del av cirkulära ekonomin. De kan spara upp till 80 procent av materialen jämfört med att tillverka en helt ny. Ändå är många konsumenter fortfarande tveksamma.

Värderingar är viktigare än nationalitet

title: We’re Investigating Prior Authorization. Help ProPublica Understand Your Health Insurance Denial.
content:
Last year, many of America’s largest health insurers vowed to reduce their use of prior authorization — the extra layer of approval insurers require before covering a medical expense. The industry’s pledge came after massive backlash to the process from patients, providers and politicians. ProPublica’s reporting has found it can delay or outright deny patients’ critical medical care.

Data as of last year shows the industry is still relying heavily on the approval process. Now, ProPublica is looking into the ways that insurers’ continued use of prior authorization is impacting patients. We need your help to figure out if prior authorization is still leading to delayed or missed treatments, tests, medical equipment or medication.

If you are covered by a plan through Medicaid, Medicare, Children’s Health Insurance Program, or the Affordable Care Act marketplace — and have had a prior authorization request delayed or denied — we want to hear from you. Your experiences help us better understand the real-life stakes of prior authorization. (For this investigation, we’re not seeking responses from people with insurance through their employer at this time.)

title: Afghanistan, 25 Years Later: Journalist Emran Feroz on the Legacy of "America's Longest War"
content:
This week marks 25 years since the U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan, the beginning of what would become the longest war in U.S. history. After installing a pro-Western government in Kabul in December 2001, U.S. and other NATO troops would remain in the country for the next two decades battling a stubborn insurgency — until a chaotic U.S. withdrawal in August 2021 that saw the Taliban return to power.

“During the 20 years of America’s longest war in Afghanistan, we could clearly see that failure was coming,” says journalist Emran Feroz, just back from a month of reporting in Afghanistan. He says the relative economic and political gains under the Western-backed government were undercut by widespread corruption and violence, particularly in rural Afghanistan. “You had torture prisons next to Burger King and KFC and Starbucks.”

content:

title: Muuttuva tartuntatautitilanne haastaa syksyn lomamatkailijoita
content:
Suomalaisten ulkomaille suuntautuva vapaa-ajanmatkailu on tyypillisesti vilkasta. Tilastokeskuksen mukaan syksyllä 2025 ulkomaan lomamatkoja tehtiin syys-joulukuussa noin 2 miljoonaa. Suomalaiset suuntaavat syyslomilla etenkin Etelä-Euroopan kohteisiin, kuten Espanjaan, Kreikkaan ja Italiaan sekä myöhemmin syksyllä Kanariansaarille ja Thaimaaseen.

"Matkailijalta vaaditaan nykyään enemmän valveutuneisuutta tartuntatautien ehkäisyssä, sillä tautitilanne voi vaihdella maailmalla nopeasti ja monet aiemmin trooppisista kohteista tutut taudit ovat levinneet myös Eurooppaan. Euroopan tautienehkäisy- ja -valvontakeskus ECDC nostaa tartuntatautiuhkia käsittelevässä raportissaan esiin useita matkailijoiden kannalta ajankohtaisia tartuntatauteja, kuten tuhkarokko sekä hyttysvälitteiset länsi-niilin virus-, chikungunya- ja dengue", kertoo vastaava sairaanhoitaja Anu Munkki Rokotepalvelusta.

Ruotsissa on käynnissä tuhkarokkoepidemia – epidemiaan liittyvä tartunta todettu myös Suomessa
